en: Puggalapaññatti Niddesa 7. The Exposition of the Designation of Persons in Groups of Seven
And how is a person one who, once submerged, remains submerged?
Here, a certain person is possessed of exclusively dark, unwholesome states.
In this way, a person is one who, once submerged, remains submerged.
And how does a person, having emerged, sink back down?
Here, a certain person emerges [with the thought]: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states;
excellent is moral dread in wholesome states; excellent is energy in wholesome states; excellent is wisdom in wholesome states. Yet he subsequently sinks back down.
His faith neither remains nor increases, but only declines; his moral shame neither remains nor increases, but only declines;
his moral dread neither remains nor increases, but only declines;
his energy neither remains nor increases, but only declines; his wisdom neither remains...
It neither increases nor decreases; it merely subsides.
Thus does a person, having emerged, sink down again.
And how does a person, having emerged, remain standing?
Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states;
excellent is moral dread in wholesome states; excellent is energy in wholesome states; excellent is wisdom in wholesome states.
His faith neither diminishes nor increases; it remains stable. His moral shame neither diminishes nor...
His sense of shame neither diminishes nor increases; it remains steady. His moral dread neither diminishes nor increases;
it remains steady. His energy neither diminishes nor increases; it remains steady. His wisdom neither diminishes nor increases;
it remains steady. In this way, a person, having emerged, remains poised.
And how does a person, having emerged, see clearly and look about?
Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states;
excellent is moral dread in wholesome states; excellent is energy in wholesome states; excellent is wisdom in wholesome states."
Thus, with the complete destruction of three fetters, he becomes a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms, fixed in destiny, and destined for full enlightenment.
In this way, a person, having emerged, practices insight and surveys.
And how does a person, having emerged, cross over?
Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states;
excellent is moral dread in wholesome states; excellent is energy in wholesome states; excellent is wisdom in wholesome states.

Through the complete destruction of three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, he becomes a once-returner who, having come back to this world only once more, makes an end of suffering.
In this way, a person, having emerged, swims across.
And how does a person, having emerged, reach a firm footing?
Here, a certain person emerges [thinking]: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states."
“Excellent is moral dread regarding wholesome states; excellent is energy regarding wholesome states; excellent is wisdom regarding wholesome states.
With the total destruction of the five lower fetters, such a person becomes one of spontaneous birth, attaining final nibbāna there, no longer subject to return from that world.
Thus, having emerged, the person has reached a firm footing.
And how does a person, having emerged, cross over, go to the further shore, and stand on dry land as a brahmin?
Here, a certain person emerges, thinking: "Excellent is faith in wholesome states; excellent is moral shame in wholesome states;
excellent is moral dread in wholesome states; excellent is energy in wholesome states; excellent is wisdom in wholesome states."

Thus, with the destruction of the taints, he dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it.
In this way, a person, having emerged, has crossed over, gone to the further shore, and stands on dry land—a brahmin.
And what kind of person is one liberated both ways?
Here, a certain person dwells having personally realized the eight liberations with the body; and having seen with wisdom, his taints are utterly destroyed.
This person is called one liberated both ways (*ubhatobhāgavimutta*).
And what kind of person is one liberated by wisdom (*paññāvimutta*)? … [as before] …
The body-witness … the one attained to vision … the one liberated by faith …
The follower by Dhamma...
And what kind of person is a follower by faith?
It is the person who, practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, has the faculty of faith predominant, and develops the Noble Path carried by faith and preceded by faith.
This person is called a follower by faith (saddhānusārī).
One who has entered the path for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry is a follower by faith; one established in the fruit is liberated by faith (saddhāvimutta).
This is the exposition of the sevenfold [classification].
